# git refresh please

Add `git refresh please`: refresh the branch and force-push it in one command. The original sketch:

```bash
$ git refresh please
# git refresh
# git please
```

After a rebase onto the trunk the branch has to be pushed with `--force-with-lease` anyway, so the two commands always come together at the end of an iteration; `done` in the flow already chains them (`git refresh && git please && git checkout $(git default)`), and this is the same pair without leaving the branch.

Expected: `git refresh please` rebases onto the tracked remote's default branch and, only if the rebase succeeded, runs `git please`; anything after `please` is handed on to `git please` (`all` / `current`).
